parts.visual:
A founder tells an investor: 'We have no competitors. We are totally unique.' The investor immediately rejects them. Why?

The Rule of Competition:
1. If you have no competitors, it means there is no market. Someone is always solving the problem right now, even if they are doing it badly.
2. The Magic Quadrant: A visual chart in a Pitch Deck showing two axes (e.g., Price vs. Quality). Your startup is always magically positioned in the 'High Quality / Low Price' top-right corner.
parts.audio: Never tell an investor that you have no competitors. It shows extreme naivety. You must conduct a brutal Competitive Analysis to prove you understand the market and exactly how you will beat the incumbents.

questions.question: A founder pitches a new software to manage HR tasks. They claim they have 'no competition'. What is the investor's immediate thought?
options: The founder hasn't done their research. Even if there isn't an exact software clone, the customer is currently using Microsoft Excel or Pen and Paper. Excel is the competitor.
The founder should raise the price.
questions.correct_answer: The founder hasn't done their research. Even if there isn't an exact software clone, the customer is currently using Microsoft Excel or Pen and Paper. Excel is the competitor.
questions.explanation: In B2B software, your biggest competitor is almost always the status quo (Excel).

questions.question: Listen to the founder explaining their 'Moat'. What is their strategy to defend against competitors?
questions.tts_text: If Google tries to copy our app, they will fail. We have spent two years signing exclusive, five-year data contracts with all the major hospitals. Google cannot get the data.
options: An 'Economic Moat' based on proprietary data and exclusive contracts. This is a highly defensible barrier to entry.
questions.correct_answer: An 'Economic Moat' based on proprietary data and exclusive contracts. This is a highly defensible barrier to entry.
questions.explanation: A good idea is not a moat. A legal monopoly on the data is a moat.

questions.question: What is the danger of the classic 'Magic Quadrant' slide in a Pitch Deck?
options: It is heavily manipulated. Every founder puts their own company in the top right corner. Investors usually ignore it unless the axes are highly specific and objective.
questions.correct_answer: It is heavily manipulated. Every founder puts their own company in the top right corner. Investors usually ignore it unless the axes are highly specific and objective.
questions.explanation: If your axes are 'Goodness' and 'Awesomeness', you will lose credibility instantly.

questions.question: What is an 'Incumbent'?
options: The massive, established corporation that currently dominates the market share (like Microsoft or Salesforce).
questions.correct_answer: The massive, established corporation that currently dominates the market share (like Microsoft or Salesforce).

questions.explanation: What every VC wants to hear: You have built a fortress.
